paper_metadata.title: Effects of molybdenum on microstructural evolution and mechanical properties in Zr–Nb alloys as nuclear fuel cladding materials
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology

evidence.quote: Effects of molybdenum on microstructural evolution and mechanical properties in Zr–Nb alloys as nuclear fuel cladding materials
The Zr–Nb alloys were modified by doping of Mo as a minor alloying element to seek for the nuclear fuel cladding materials with better characteristics.

An arc melting apparatus was employed to prepare experimental alloys under high purity argon atmosphere. For each button ingot preparation, the melting process was repeated three times to homogenize the chemical composition.
The bulk specimens cutting from the button ingots (5 mm thick) were β-phase quenched, the quenching rate was roughly estimated as the order of 500–1000 K/s.
Then, cold working (CW) and annealing were performed for three times to make the thickness of specimen into 1 mm.
Final annealing was performed at 873 K for 24 hours in order to attain the fully recrystallized microstructure.

evidence.section: 3.1. Effects of Mo on microstructure after the beta-phase quenching
evidence.quote: the microstructure of Zr–Nb–Mo alloys in this study after the β-phase quenching was composed of the lath martensites and the lens martensites

evidence.section: 3.1. Effects of Mo on microstructure after the beta-phase quenching
evidence.quote: The lens martensite, also called plate martensite or acicular martensite, was filled with twinning-like lamellae with the size of several tens of nanometer.
